topPRs.title: justfile: refactor `release-notes` to add `release-paths` which can be used by scripts and skills
topPRs.author: pauldowman
topPRs.body:
## Description

`just release-notes <component>` held an inline `case` mapping each component to git-cliff `--include-path` args. The proofs release tooling had duplication of this list. 

This extracts the list into a `release-paths <component>` recipe, so it is defined once, here, next to the code it describes. `release-notes` reads it; so does the external tooling, which stops keeping a copy.

Output is one `<label><TAB><path>` pair per line. Consecutive lines sharing a label are a group — a set of paths that ship as one unit, such as a bundled binary's dependency closure or the shared Go infrastructure. A consumer that sections its output groups by label; one that only needs the path set reads column 2. Both views come from one stream, so a component's paths and their grouping cannot disagree.

### Behavior changes

| component | change |
|---|---|
| op-node, op-batcher, op-proposer, op-supernode, op-reth, op-deployer, op-contracts | **none** |
| **op-dispute-mon** | now supported — previously fell through to the error branch, and its release notes were assembled by hand |
| **op-challenger** | gains `cannon/` and kona-host's dependency closure |
| **`kona-*`** | gains `rust/op-revm/` |

op-challenger's is the substantive fix. Its image ships three binaries — `op-challenger`, `cannon`, and `kona-host` built from the in-repo `rust/` workspace (see the `op-challenger-target` stage in `ops/docker/op-stack-go/Dockerfile`) — but only the first was in its include paths. A kona-host-only fix has no `op-challenger/` diff and so could never appear in its release notes, while still changing what operators run. #22732 was exactly that shape: a genesis-offset bug that hung every interop VM-runner run against OP Mainnet. For `v1.9.3..v1.9.4` the notes go from 66 PRs to 111.

The `kona-*` arms stay deliberately wide (all of `rust/kona/`) so this PR does not narrow kona's own notes; the precise per-binary closure is used only where it is needed, for op-challenger's bundled kona-host.

## Tests

- For every component that existed before, the reconstructed `--include-path` args are character-for-character identical to the old `case` output.
- `just release-notes op-node v1.19.3 v1.19.4` is byte-identical to `develop`.
- `just release-notes op-dispute-mon v1.5.2 v1.5.3` now produces notes instead of an error.
- An unknown component exits non-zero and lists the valid ones.

## Additional context

The external consumer is the `proofs-release-rc` / `proofs-release-finalize` tooling, which reads this recipe rather than keeping its own list, and drops both its op-dispute-mon workaround and the per-release step that reconciled the two lists by hand.
